interpretation: The updated screen is a comparison of businesses, not a single pipeline trade. All 35active listings have November 13daily observations, and 15vendor quarter fields advanced since the November 4batch. The unchanged complete-input ranking now starts with ProFrac, Liberty and Expand. ProFrac's rise from third to first is not proof of a new edge: it is a cyclical services business, and its issuer release highlights financing constraints. Negative-EBITDA NFE still scores highly in the raw ranking, which illustrates why incomplete-input rows cannot set the headline.

Energy Transfer now has usable vendor EV and enters the complete-input group at fifth. NGL leaves that group because the provider reported-growth field is unavailable; it is not replaced with another growth calculation. The other input exceptions remain visible. A score can also change because the peer normalization changes, so rank movement is not attributed solely to an issuer's fundamentals.

The infrastructure evidence remains more nuanced than a gas-spread chart. Targa reported stronger volumes and 18% adjusted-EBITDA growth; Kinetik reported 1.61x dividend coverage using its own definition. Western Midstream's growth spending produced negative free cash flow after distributions despite strong DCF. Contract cashflows can be valuable, but debt, project spending, counterparties and refinancing are still part of the equity thesis.

The TTF leg remains historical: its latest observed level is November 13, yet no new consecutive daily pair has formed beyond July 2. The original 180-valid-observation beta still ends July 2. JKM beta does reach November 13. No gas price was carried across the missing interval, and an isolated quote was not turned into a one-day change. Three-factor scores remain provisional rather than a validated current hedge or causal relationship.

issuer_primary_context.source_policy: Primary issuer releases and issuer SEC exhibits only. Issuer-defined adjusted results, distributions and guidance are context, never replacements for vendor scoring fields. Native HTTP failures are retained; web-source verification is separately identified.

entries.summary: ProFrac reported about $1.05bn principal debt and $1.01bn net debt at quarter-end, with about $79m remaining ABL availability. It is pursuing liquidity and debt-reduction initiatives whose completion is uncertain. This strengthens the financing countercase to a high reset/value score; the business is completion services, not pipeline toll rent.

Targa reported $1.504bn adjusted EBITDA, up 18% year over year, and record Permian/NGL transport and fractionation volumes. Its expected 20% increase in the 2027 common dividend is a forward-looking expectation, separate from the current $1.25 quarterly declaration. Growth supports the infrastructure thesis, while valuation and project funding still matter.

Kinetik reported $278.1m adjusted EBITDA and $213.7m distributable cash flow. Its issuer-defined dividend coverage was 1.61x and credit-agreement leverage 3.70x. Those definitions include specific adjustments and are distinct from the vendor net-debt/EBITDA ratio. Capacity additions and contract rollover offer growth, with financing and execution as countercases.

Western Midstream reported $708.3m adjusted EBITDA, $512.3m distributable cash flow and a $0.930 quarterly distribution per unit. Free cash flow after distributions was negative $148.5m amid growth spending. Strong throughput does not remove the need to distinguish distribution coverage, growth capex and external funding.

Kodiak raised full-year adjusted EBITDA and discretionary cash flow guidance. It reported compression-infrastructure revenue of $318.4m and power-infrastructure revenue of $42.0m. This is compression and power-service capacity exposure, with equipment utilization, financing and customer demand risks rather than direct ownership of an LNG price spread.

Vistra reported $2.378bn ongoing-operations adjusted EBITDA. Its release describes liquidity of about $5.4bn pro forma after preferred-stock redemption, acquisition cash payments and debt repayment. Power scarcity and acquisitions can support earnings while changing financing needs; unrealized hedge gains are not interchangeable with current operating cash flow.

Flex LNG declared $0.75 per share for the third quarter, with payment expected around December 10. This is a declared distribution, not proof of sustainable free cash flow. The vendor annual cashflow table still lacks a usable capex item, so annual FCF/EV remains unavailable in the unchanged screen.

The issuer filing covers the quarter and six months ended September 30. The fresh vendor record still lacks revenueGrowth, so the score retains its original neutral missing-factor treatment and NGL is excluded from the complete-input headline. Filing availability does not authorize replacing that field with a different growth calculation.
